subject: Relay affinity change notice — request for inventory + targeted audit pack
messages:
From: EdgeLoom Ops <ops@edgeloom.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Sable Legal <contracts@sablelegal.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 15:22:00 +0100
Subject: Notice: temporary relay affinity shift and subprocessor roster

Hi Michael,

We wanted to notify Redwood Inference of a short-term routing adjustment that will affect traffic originating from our EU edge cluster. Due to an urgent maintenance window at our primary EU POP, some customer traffic will be routed via our backup relay pool in Frankfurt and Amsterdam for ~72 hours starting 2026-09-20 02:00 UTC. The change is purely operational; however, because the backup pool is operated by a different subprocessor (EdgeLoom Relay Services Ltd.), we are sharing the roster and the minimal evidence package now.

Attached: edgeloom_subprocessor_roster_20260919.csv (roles, jurisdictions), edgeloom_routing_diagram_v2.png, edgeloom_affinity_notice.pdf

Quick notes: 
- No customer data is stored on the relay tier — relays perform ephemeral TCP/TLS proxying and KV-pass-through only.
- All relays use AES-256 for in-flight and at-rest logs; KMS control remains with EdgeLoom (key jurisdiction: IE).
- We are passing along a one-page SOC2 summary and our standard subprocessors appendix to Sable Legal in cc.

Action requested from Redwood: please confirm whether you require an onshore fallback (we can pin routing to your on-prem or Dedicated capacity) or whether you accept the temporary EU-relay routing under the existing DPA. If you need additional evidence (full SOC2 report, live egress diagrams, signed attestations) let us know and we will queue a targeted audit pack.

We appreciate a reply by EOD 2026-09-24 so we can finalize routing. Happy to jump on a short call if useful.

Best,
Alex Mercer
Operations Manager — EdgeLoom
ops@edgeloom.com

--- Attachment stubs: edgeloom_subprocessor_roster_20260919.csv (CSV), edgeloom_routing_diagram_v2.png (PNG), edgeloom_affinity_notice.pdf (PDF)
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: EdgeLoom Ops <ops@edgeloom.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 18:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: temporary relay affinity shift and subprocessor roster

Alex —

Thanks for the heads-up and for sending the roster. A few immediate clarifying asks from our side so we can triage the compliance impact quickly:

1) Please provide a complete, machine-readable subprocessor inventory for the backup relay pool that includes: role, country of operation, full legal entity name, data processing purpose, and KMS jurisdiction per entity. The CSV we received is a good start but missing legal names and KMS endpoints.

2) We need a network-level egress diagram that shows whether any telemetry/observability streams from relays cross additional third parties (e.g., cloud logging providers). Call out where logs are persisted and for how long.

3) If you have a signed attestation for AES-256 keys and KMS control (IE jurisdiction), attach it. If not, provide an estimated delivery date for certs and the SOC2 summary/report.

4) Please confirm whether any subprocessor in the backup pool performs user-data transformation (LLM input normalization, enrichment, tokenization) or whether the relays are strictly TCP/TLS pass-through. If transformation occurs, we need the sample processing flow and retention windows.

Operational ask: if the backup pool will be in use for >48 hours, Redwood may request an onshore fallback pin (route traffic to our Dedicated nodes) while we review. Give us an earliest window for validation and we'll coordinate with our networking team.

We may request a targeted audit pack (company-level SOC2 + relay-level network diagrams + KMS attestation). If you expect to supply that, please indicate scope and delivery ETA.

CC'ing Laura (privacy/compliance) and Marissa (customer success) for intake and Ben (security) for review.

Target due date for the evidence: 2026-09-24 EOD. If you can do sooner, we can avoid an onshore pin.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Head of Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference

---
Michael Grant
Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.com

From: EdgeLoom Ops <ops@edgeloom.com>

Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 09:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Notice: temporary relay affinity shift and subprocessor roster

On Sun, 19 Sep 2026 at 18:40 -0700 Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex —
>
> Thanks for the heads-up and for sending the roster. A few immediate clarifying asks from our side so we can triage the compliance impact quickly:
>
> 1) Please provide a complete, machine-readable subprocessor inventory for the backup relay pool that includes: role, country of operation, full legal entity name, data processing purpose, and KMS jurisdiction per entity. The CSV we received is a good start but missing legal names and KMS endpoints.
>
> 2) We need a network-level egress diagram that shows whether any telemetry/observability streams from relays cross additional third parties (e.g., cloud logging providers). Call out where logs are persisted and for how long.

Alex Mercer <ops@edgeloom.com> replied:

Hi Michael —

Thanks, understood. We can provide the expanded inventory and a “relay-level” audit pack. Quick answers inline:
- Relays are strictly proxying—no transformation, no tokenization. We will include a signed attestation stating that explicitly.
- KMS keys are held by EdgeLoom Ireland Ltd. (IE) — we will add the KMS endpoints in the CSV.
- Telemetry: relays forward minimal connection telemetry to GrafanaCloud (logs retained 7 days) and a separate anonymized metrics stream to CloudMetrics Inc (30 days).

Attachments: we are pushing a follow-up package to Sable Legal (SOC2 extract + relay_attestation.pdf) by EOD 2026-09-20.

If it helps, we propose a 30-minute call Monday 2026-09-21 16:00 CET to walk through the diagrams and answer any live questions.

Regards,
Alex Mercer
Operations Manager — EdgeLoom

Thanks Alex — appreciate the quick turnaround and the proposed call.

I confirmed with Laura and Ben: we still need the expanded CSV and the relay_attestation.pdf before the call; please upload to the drive link below or attach to the thread so legal can triage.

Drive link for secure evidence upload: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cEdgeLoomAuditPack

I've tentatively accepted the 2026-09-21 16:00 CET slot on our calendar; Marissa will lead the customer-impact checklist on the call.

Also attaching Redwood's subprocessor questionnaire template (template attached as stub) — if you can pre-fill the document for relay entries ahead of the call, we'll focus on the egress/telemetry items during the session. If the audit pack contains redlines or restricted items, Sable Legal can follow up after the call.

If the evidence cannot be provided by EOD 2026-09-20 as indicated, please confirm an exact ETA; depending on the timing we may request an onshore fallback pin while we finish review.
